_note: One unit = one lesson path in five steps. Write 'God' (the Muslim view shows 'Allah'). Verses by ref only (shown from src/data/ayahs.json); hadith by id only (shown from src/data/hadith.json). 'about' lines are our own words, never a translation.

intro.muslim: Musa led the Children of Israel out of Egypt by night. At sunrise they reached the sea, with Pharaoh's army closing in behind them. The people cried: we are caught! Watch what Musa said.
intro.curious: Musa, known in the Bible as Moses, led his people out of Egypt by night. At sunrise they reached the sea, with Pharaoh's army closing in behind. The people cried: we are caught! Watch what Musa said.

muslim.situation: You have a big assessment at school tomorrow and you're anxious.

options.label: Don't revise: whatever God wills will happen.
options.feedback: Trust without effort isn't what Islam teaches. Musa was told to strike the sea with his staff: he had to act.

options.label: Prepare as well as you can, make dua, then rest and leave the result to God.
options.feedback: That's tawakkul. Do your part fully, like the birds that go out each morning, and leave the outcome to Him.

options.label: Stay up all night panicking over every possible outcome.
options.feedback: Worry doesn't change the result. Musa's words at the sea show another way.

options.label: Prepare, but keep worrying anyway.
options.feedback: The preparation is right. The next step is to let the result go to God.

curious.situation: You have something big tomorrow, an interview or an important presentation, and you're anxious.

options.label: Don't prepare: whatever happens, happens.
options.feedback: Islam teaches the opposite: do your part, then trust. Even the birds go out each morning to find their food.

options.label: Prepare as well as you can, then rest and let go of the result.
options.feedback: That's close to tawakkul: do your part fully, then leave the outcome to God.

options.label: Stay up all night worrying about every outcome.
options.feedback: Worry doesn't change the result. Musa's words at the sea show another way.

options.label: Prepare, but keep worrying anyway.
options.feedback: The preparation is right. Tawakkul is the next step: letting the result go.

heading.muslim: What God teaches about trusting Him
heading.curious: What Islam teaches about trust in God

quran.about: When the people cry that they are overtaken, Musa answers: no, my Lord is with me, He will guide me.
God tells Musa to strike the sea with his staff, and it parts.
Whoever relies on God, He is enough for them.
Once you have decided, rely on God; God loves those who rely on Him.
Yaqub advises his sons to enter the city by different gates, then says: upon Him I rely. He takes precautions and trusts God.

hadith.about: God provides for those who truly rely on Him, as He provides for the birds. Notice that the birds still go out each morning: effort and trust go together.

insights.text: Musa still had to walk to the sea and strike it with his staff (26:63). Trust in God is not sitting still; it is doing your part, then relying on Him for the result.
The birds in the hadith (Tirmidhi 2344) don't stay in their nests: they go out hungry in the morning. God provides for them through their going out.

check.q: What did the people cry when they saw Pharaoh's army?
check.why: They cried that they were overtaken (26:61).

options: No! My Lord is with me; He will guide me
check.why: My Lord is with me; He will guide me (26:62).

check.q: What did God tell Musa to do?
options: Strike the sea with his staff
check.why: Strike the sea with your staff, and it parted (26:63).

check.q: In the saying about the birds, what do the birds do each morning?
options: Wait in the nest to be fed
Go out hungry to seek their food
Store up food for the year
check.why: They go out hungry in the morning and return full in the evening: effort and trust together.

check.q: What does 65:3 promise to those who rely on God?
check.why: Whoever relies upon God, He is sufficient for them.

reflection.muslim: What are you worried about this week? Write down what's in your hands, do it, then hand the rest to God in dua.
reflection.curious: What's worrying you this week? Which part of it is in your hands, and which part could you let go?
